newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-BP shares up as profits beat forecasts.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-BP shares up as profits beat forecasts.

text.p: Shares in British Petroleum Co Plc climbed on Tuesday after the oil giant reported first quarter results sharply ahead of market forecasts.

Boosted by higher oil prices, increased volumes and cost reductions, net earnings before exceptional items rose by 19 percent to 755 million pounds ($1.2 billion) from 633 million a year ago. In dollar terms, earnings in the quarter rose by 27 percent.
Analysts, whose expectations had centred around 690 million pounds, noted that the performance was strong across BP's range of operations, as well as showing progress towards efficiency targets.

"The results are very good...better in every segment," said Dresdner Kleinwort Benson analyst Paul Spedding. "It's important to note that it's not just (higher) oil prices -- it's also refining and chemicals."
BP's shares, meanwhile, closed 29 pence higher at 732-1/2 pence.
Finance director John Buchanan said BP will likely exceed its 1997 target of achieving $300 million of underlying performance improvements from productivity gains and cost savings.
These gains and savings already totalled $120 million in the first quarter of 1997.
Buchanan added he expected net overall savings for BP from its European downstream venture with Mobil Corp to start coming in in the second half of this year at between $50 million to &100 million.
Adding to these upbeat comments, Chief Executive John Browne said BP is looking to substantially boost its share of oil production in the Gulf of Mexico -- the current hot spot for the oil industry.
BP aims to raise its share in the region's oil production ventures to 300,000 barrels per day by 2005 from a current level of 80,000.
The company said higher oil prices and volumes led to a 24 percent increase in first-quarter upstream earnings to a record 913 million pounds.
Oil and gas production rose by 3.5 percent in the quarter to a six-year high of 1.601 million barrels of oil equivalent per day.
The commissioning of the North Sea Harding and Andrew fields and the Mars field in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico, together with strong gas sales in Britain, were largely responsible for the rise.
Oil prices have fallen back after a strong start to the year, and BP said price prospects will be influenced over the coming months by increases in production.
But the oil giant added the recent weakening of prices may lead to some further improvement in downstream margins.

In chemicals, the result was down by 19 percent, reflecting the effect of the weak mark and lower underlying margins. But BP said the outcome still represented an 18 percent return on capital. ($ = 0.618 British Pounds)
